scenarios.title: Use each author-entry control on the home page to reach the publishing packages page
scenarios.intent: Prove that a visitor can use either author-entry control on the home page and reach the publishing packages page in both cases.
scenarios.technique_notes: Applied happy-path coverage and equivalence partitioning. Grouped `Start Publishing` and `Compare all packages →` as equivalent-control variation because both source-grounded controls promise the same `/publish` outcome and changing the selected control should not change the outcome family. No boundary, negative, covering-array, or dependency expansion applied because there is no constrained input, no outcome-changing combination, and no prerequisite state. Budget ceiling 8 applied; this scenario ranked 1/3 and was kept with no eviction.

scenarios.title: Use the published-books browse link on the home page to reach the catalog page
scenarios.intent: Prove that a visitor can leave the home page for the published-books showcase through the dedicated browse link and land on `/books`.
scenarios.technique_notes: Applied happy-path coverage. Kept this as a distinct scenario because the source promises a different destination family (`/books`) from the author-entry controls, so the selected link changes the outcome. No equivalence-class parameters, boundary, negative, covering-array, or dependency expansion applied because the route has one control and one expected outcome with no constrained input. Budget ceiling 8 applied; this scenario ranked 2/3 and was kept with no eviction.

scenarios.title: Inspect the home page discovery content and preview sections
scenarios.intent: Prove that one home-page visit shows the required discovery content: the exact heading, the catalog-size statement, all four package previews with their promised commercial fields, and four recently published book tiles.
scenarios.technique_notes: Applied happy-path coverage by consolidating the read-only render promises that hold on first load, and applied equivalence partitioning to the package previews because each of the four cards is promised to expose the same field family (name, tagline, price, and `View package` link). No boundary, negative, covering-array, or dependency expansion applied because this path has no user input or outcome-changing combinations. Budget ceiling 8 applied; this scenario ranked 3/3 and was kept with no eviction.

judgements.rationale: Highest value because it covers both home-page author-entry controls that route visitors into the revenue-driving publishing flow; a broken route strands the primary conversion path.
High value because it covers the home-page route into the published-books showcase, the second half of the platform's discovery promise.
High value because it covers the bulk of the public discovery content in one visit, but static render issues are slightly less critical than broken navigation routes.
